raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes a 3-5% decode regression in v0.32.0, caused by #56891.

#56891 changed automatic FlashInfer allreduce selection to use `trtllm` for every node-local process group. Before it, single-node runs used `mnnvl`, falling back to `trtllm` on nodes without NVSwitch multicast. The PR included no perf data, and on single-node NVSwitch systems `trtllm` is slower.

## Evidence

The perf-eval nightlies show a step in the 14 commits between the 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04 nightlies, and #56891 is the only distributed change among them. Only TP>1 workloads moved:

| workload | before (10-03) | after (10-04 on) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200 | ~5650 tok/s, TPOT 20.8 ms | ~5460 tok/s, TPOT 21.6 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP4, H200 (same host) | 10883 tok/s, TPOT 11.20 ms | 10571 tok/s, TPOT 11.54 ms |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200 | ~2770 tok/s | ~2650-2720 tok/s |
| MiniMax-M3 TP8, H200 | TPOT 35.9 ms | TPOT 36.8 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1, B200 | unchanged | unchanged |

A/B on the v0.32.0rc2 image with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` forced:

| workload | default (`trtllm`) | `mnnvl` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200, 8k/1k conc 128 | 5462 tok/s, TPOT 21.78 ms | **5728 tok/s, TPOT 20.22 ms** |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200, 3 repeats | 2533 / 2753 / 2771 tok/s | **2581 / 2811 / 2845 tok/s** |

## Change

For node-local groups, auto-selection goes back to `mnnvl` with `allow_trtllm_fallback=True`. The existing fallback still builds a `trtllm` workspace when `mnnvl` can't create one (no NVSwitch multicast). Multi-node selection from #56891 is unchanged: `mnnvl` on Blackwell, disabled on Hopper. The unit test's expectations are updated to match.

cc @elvircrn: is there a case where single-node `mnnvl` misbehaved that #56891 was fixing? The PR description only covers the multi-node cases.

## Test Plan

- `test_flashinfer_auto_backend_uses_group_topology` updated for the single-node cases.
- ruff check/format pass.
- Perf A/B above (perf-eval build 680).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

LGTM. This aligns with my impression that mnnvl is generally faster than trtllm backend. I am not sure why default was switched from mnnvl to trtllm. If it is due to functional issues, we should investigate the cause. Otherwise I agree we should switch it back for performance.

files.patch:
@@ -462,8 +462,8 @@ def test_flashinfer_standalone_workspace_size(
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(
     ("node_count", "is_blackwell", "expected"),
     [
-        (1, False, ("trtllm", False)),
-        (1, True, ("trtllm", False)),
+        (1, False, ("mnnvl", True)),
+        (1, True, ("mnnvl", True)),
         (2, False, (None, False)),
         (2, True, ("mnnvl", False)),
     ],

@@ -156,10 +156,12 @@ def _resolve_fi_ar_backend(group: ProcessGroup) -> tuple[str | None, bool]:
 
     node_count = _node_count(group)
     if node_count == 1:
-        # TRTLLM supports single-node allreduce on Hopper and Blackwell. Do not
-        # create an MNNVL workspace when the process group is node-local.
-        backend = "trtllm"
-        allow_trtllm_fallback = False
+        # MNNVL decodes faster than TRTLLM on single-node NVSwitch systems
+        # (about 3-5% throughput at TP4/TP8 on H200 and B200). Fall back to
+        # TRTLLM where the node lacks NVSwitch multicast and MNNVL cannot
+        # create its workspace.
+        backend = "mnnvl"
+        allow_trtllm_fallback = True
     elif current_platform.has_device_capability(100):
         # MNNVL requires Blackwell-class GPUs and is the only supported
         # FlashInfer backend for a multi-node allreduce process group.
